title: What Happens When a Dryer Vent Is Blocked?
h1: What Happens When a Dryer Vent Is Blocked?
description: A blocked dryer vent makes loads take longer, overheats the dryer, adds moisture to your home and raises the risk of a lint fire. Learn the signs and causes.
quick_answer: When a dryer vent is blocked, hot, moist air can't leave the house. Clothes take longer to dry, the dryer and laundry room get hot, and lint builds up even faster. The dryer can overheat and wear out parts, and lint near heat is a fire risk. A gas dryer with a blocked vent can also push carbon monoxide indoors.
body:
Your dryer works by pulling in room air, heating it, tumbling it through wet clothes and pushing it outside through the vent. Every load sends lint along with that air. The lint screen catches most of it, but some always gets through and sticks inside the vent. Over time, that narrows the path until the air can barely get out.

What are the first signs of a blocked dryer vent?

  • Clothes need a second cycle or come out damp
  • The top of the dryer or the clothes feel unusually hot
  • The laundry room feels warm and humid while the dryer runs
  • A burning or musty smell during a cycle
  • Lint collecting around the door, behind the dryer or at the outside vent
  • The outside flap barely opens, or you feel weak airflow outside

If you notice more than one of these, the vent likely needs attention.

What does a blocked vent do to the dryer?

With nowhere to go, heat builds up inside the machine. Dryers have safety parts like a high limit thermostat and a thermal fuse that cut the heat when things get too hot. A restricted vent makes those parts work constantly, and a blown thermal fuse is a common result. The heating element, gas burner, blower and motor all run longer and hotter than they should.

Many repair calls for a dryer that runs but won't heat trace back to the vent.

Is a blocked dryer vent a fire hazard?

Yes. Lint is very flammable, and a blocked vent puts lint and high heat in the same place for longer. Fires can start inside the dryer or in the vent itself, sometimes in a wall or attic where you can't see them. Never run the dryer while you're asleep or away if you suspect a clog.

Can a blocked vent cause carbon monoxide problems?

With a gas dryer, yes. Gas dryers produce combustion gases, including carbon monoxide, that are meant to leave through the vent. A blocked or disconnected vent can push them back into the home. Every home with gas appliances should have working carbon monoxide alarms. If an alarm sounds, get everyone outside and call 911.

What else does a blocked vent affect?

All the moisture from wet clothes has to go somewhere. When the vent is blocked or disconnected, it ends up in the laundry room, garage or wall cavity. That can lead to:

  • Condensation and mildew around the laundry area
  • Damp drywall or framing where the vent runs
  • Higher indoor humidity, which is already common near the coast
  • Higher energy use, since each load takes more time

What causes dryer vents to get blocked?

  1. Lint buildup over months and years of use
  2. Crushed or kinked transition hoses behind the dryer when it's pushed against the wall
  3. Long vent runs with many turns, where lint collects at each elbow
  4. Roof terminations, common in condos and two-story homes, where air has to push lint upward
  5. Bird and rodent nests in the outside vent hood
  6. Stuck or painted-over flaps on the outside cap
  7. Screens on the vent cap, which catch lint and clog quickly. Screens don't belong on dryer vent caps.
  8. Foil or vinyl flex hose, whose ridges trap lint and which crushes easily

What should you do about a blocked dryer vent?

If you suspect a serious clog, stop using the dryer until it's checked, especially if you smell burning.

Start with the easy checks. Clean the lint screen every load. Pull the dryer out and look for a crushed or disconnected hose. Go outside while the dryer runs and feel for strong, warm airflow.

If airflow is weak, the blockage is inside the vent, often in a wall, attic or roof run that's hard to reach. A professional cleaning clears the full length of the vent from both ends, checks the cap and connections and tests airflow afterward. faqs: How often should a dryer vent be cleaned?
Once a year is a common guideline for most homes. Large families, long vent runs and roof vents may need it more often. If drying times creep up, don't wait for the yearly cleaning.
Can I clean my dryer vent myself?

You can clean the lint screen, the area under it and a short, straight vent with a brush kit. Long runs, roof vents and vents inside walls are harder to clean fully, and pushing a brush too hard can disconnect sections inside the wall.
Why does my dryer stop heating?
A common cause is a blown thermal fuse or tripped high limit, often due to overheating from a restricted vent. Replacing the part without clearing the vent usually means it will fail again.
Is a blocked dryer vent dangerous with an electric dryer?
Yes. Electric dryers don't produce carbon monoxide, but the fire risk from lint and heat applies to both electric and gas dryers.
